name: Matrix Determinant Disguise
description: The constraint that two connected nodes must have different values (1 and 2) is disguised as a linear algebra property. Each link defines a 2x2 symmetric matrix using the state values of its endpoints. The requirement that the matrix be invertible (non-zero determinant) mathematically simplifies to the difference of their squares being non-zero, which for values in {1, 2} strictly enforces that the two states must be different. This forces models to perform algebraic reasoning to deduce the bipartite coloring structure.
